text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-The high Lebanese-Syrian Committee grouping ministers from both sides will meet in Damascus today to adopt the resolutions of the committee's January 12 meeting.
-Saudi Arabian Airlines will resume flights to Beirut in February after a halt of nearly 15 years due to the civil war in Lebanon.
-U.S. ambassador to Lebanon Jones said he expects progress in the Arab-Israeli peace process within the coming few months.

-Chairman of privately-owned Lebanese Broadcasting Corporation International (LBCI) Pierre Daher said the private television will start today its satellite broadcasting to Europe under the name LBC Europe.
-Israeli forces shell suspected positions of pro-Iranian Hizbollah guerrillas in Iqlim al-Toufah ridge in south Lebanon.
-Lebanon's highest court sentenced to death the head of a small radical Sunni Moslem group and three supporters for the 1995 killing of a rival Islamic cleric.
-For the third time in two weeks, a masked gunman killed a a member of Palestinian guerrilla group in a south Lebanon refugee camp.
-Lebanon's U.N. ambassador presented a request from Beirut asking for the renewal of the mandate of the UNIFIL peacekeeping mission in south Lebanon for another six months.
